chapter: Louis Metcalf and leading his own bands
title: Stretch Carl Ridley and why he gives soloists room
summary: Caldwell praised young tenor Carl Ridley, said many good players stay hidden, and explained he prefers to feature his men.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: (Unintelligible) he's one of my young (unintelligible). He's -- in '73 -- he worked with Benny Carter -- good tenor man. And he's about -- Stretch is about -- then practically six feet. So I told Stretch, I said, come on, you're playing potentates ball tonight, tomorrow, next Friday. Hi, Hap. I'd say, look, tell you in front, I don't want you to be cutting me on them solos. And that would tickle him to death, you know.
(Laughter)
And I'd say --
What was he saying? The nickname -- Ridley
"Stretch", Carl, "Stretch" (unintelligible) -- they called him Stretch because he was so tall.
Yes.
He played with Benny Carter and all of them, good tenor player.
I didn't catch your second name.
Carl Ridley.
Carl Ridley.
Yeah, we called him Stretch because he's tall.
But I mean do you mean that he was -- was he not a good soloist?
He was a good soloist.
Well, what way did he play?
He was featured with Benny Carter. He went all over the West Coast with Benny and all.
I never heard of him.

Yeah, well, there are a lot of fellows get hidden behind certain things, you know. They never was pushed to the front. Just like you have maybe four, five in the reeds. Maybe this guy had been in a little longer and you're the lead tenor man, so wouldn't bother, you got the tenor man playing first, on playing fourth tenor, fifth baritone, first alto, third alto. These guys, I'd give the lead, you play what you want, but you got a guy been playing with you longer, so you feature him more than with the other man. But with me, I said, 'you got to play, man. Go on.'
Well, I think that's absolutely (unintelligible).
We'd have a (unintelligible) get together, say, we're going to have a fight now. Say, what? You're all (unintelligible) in on the bandstand. I'm always
in the bandstand. You take four, I'm going to take four. And if you get smart, I'm going to get smart on you. Just kidding like that, you know, play, played good, and they enjoy them more. You know.
